Store an array with its shape and dtype

Use .npy for one array and .npz to store several named arrays. Load numerical files with allow_pickle=False, and avoid object arrays in files you plan to exchange. Use a context manager when opening .npz archives.

from io import BytesIO
import numpy as np

buffer = BytesIO()
np.save(buffer, np.array([[2, 3]], dtype=np.int16))
buffer.seek(0)
a = np.load(buffer, allow_pickle=False)
print(a.shape, a.dtype.name)
Example output
(1, 2) int16

Read straightforward numeric text

loadtxt suits regularly shaped numeric text. Set the delimiter and skip header rows. Try genfromtxt when you need missing-value handling, or pandas when columns have names, mixed types, or richer parsing needs.

from io import StringIO
import numpy as np

data = StringIO("units,price\n2,3.5\n4,2.0\n")
a = np.loadtxt(data, delimiter=",", skiprows=1)
print(a.tolist())
Example output
[[2.0, 3.5], [4.0, 2.0]]
